items.explanation: ORR-1 b grades each Basel II Level 1 event type on frequency and loss severity. Placing all seven shows that no category is rated rare but severe, and that the two categories with high severity (CPBP very high, EDPM high) are exactly the process- and client-driven ones rated high frequency.

tiles.evidence: liquidity facility availability, and unrestricted deposits

tiles.why: Restricted liquidity (medium horizon, partly available) covers e.g. collateralization.
tiles.evidence: collateralization requirements

tiles.text: Reserved for purposes arising within normal operations

items.pattern: Only the short-term contingent buffer reaches the top row: availability under stress does not rise with horizon, and operational and strategic liquidity sit at opposite ends of the horizon axis yet both at the bottom of availability.

pattern_evidence.text: Only contingent liquidity is freely available

items.explanation: LTR-9 lays the four uses of funding liquidity on two axes: short- to long-term funding, and not available to available under a stress test. Contingent liquidity is the only freely available one; restricted is attributed to specific outflows; strategic is not meant for daily operations, although its high-quality asset portion does contribute to contingent funding.
